options.C: Professional competence and due care
options.D: Integrity

questions.explanation: Confidentiality requires accountants to respect the confidentiality of information acquired through professional and business relationships. They should be alert to the risk of inadvertent disclosure, including in social settings and to close friends or family. Disclosing a client's financial difficulties without authority is a breach.

questions.question_text: An ICAEW member posts comments on social media mocking a former client and making unsupported claims that a rival firm's partners are incompetent. Which fundamental principle is most directly breached?

options.A: Objectivity
options.B: Professional competence and due care
options.C: Independence
options.D: Professional behaviour

questions.explanation: Professional behaviour requires accountants to comply with relevant laws and regulations and avoid any conduct that might discredit the profession. Making disparaging and unsupported claims about others, or mocking clients publicly, could discredit the profession. Depending on the content, confidentiality may also be at risk.

questions.question_text: The ICAEW Code of Ethics is divided into parts. Which part specifically deals with professional accountants in business?

options.A: Part 1
options.B: Part 2
options.C: Part 3
options.D: Part 4A

questions.explanation: Part 1 sets out the fundamental principles and conceptual framework and applies to all professional accountants. Part 2 applies to professional accountants in business, and Part 3 to professional accountants in public practice. Parts 4A and 4B set out independence requirements for audit and review engagements and for other assurance engagements respectively.

questions.question_text: An accountant leaves a firm and joins a competitor. Which statement about the duty of confidentiality is correct?

options.A: The duty ends as soon as the employment ends
options.B: The duty continues after the relationship ends, although the accountant may use general experience and expertise gained
options.C: The duty ends after one year unless renewed in writing
options.D: The duty applies only to information about listed clients

questions.explanation: The Code states that the duty of confidentiality continues even after the end of a relationship between an accountant and a client or employer. The accountant can use the general knowledge and experience gained, but must not use or disclose confidential information acquired during the previous role.

questions.question_text: An audit senior leaves an unencrypted laptop containing client payroll files on a train. Which of the following is the most significant risk arising from this accidental disclosure?

options.A: The firm's audit fee for the client will automatically be reduced
options.B: The client's financial statements will automatically be qualified
options.C: Personal data could be misused, causing harm to individuals and exposing the firm to regulatory sanctions, legal claims and reputational damage
options.D: There is no risk because the disclosure was accidental

questions.explanation: Accidental disclosure of confidential and personal data can harm the individuals concerned, for example through identity theft, and can lead to regulatory penalties under data protection law, legal claims and loss of client trust. The fact that the disclosure was unintentional does not remove these risks. Firms reduce such risks through encryption and data security policies.

questions.question_text: An accountant in practice discovers that a client is involved in money laundering. Which statement about disclosure of this information is correct?

options.A: Disclosure is required by law, so reporting it in line with anti-money laundering legislation does not breach the principle of confidentiality
options.B: The accountant must not disclose the information because of the duty of confidentiality
options.C: The accountant may disclose only if the client gives permission
options.D: The accountant should post the information publicly to warn others

questions.explanation: The Code recognises that disclosure may be required by law, for example under anti-money laundering legislation. In the UK, an accountant in the regulated sector must report knowledge or suspicion of money laundering, usually via the firm's money laundering reporting officer. Asking the client's permission would risk tipping off, and public disclosure is not appropriate.

questions.question_text: A client asks its accountant to provide copies of its financial records directly to its bank to support a loan application. Under which circumstance may the accountant disclose this confidential information?

options.A: Disclosure is required by a court order
options.B: Disclosure is required by anti-money laundering law
options.C: Disclosure is permitted because the client has authorised it
options.D: Disclosure is never permitted to third parties

questions.explanation: Confidential information may be disclosed when it is permitted by law and authorised by the client or employer. Here, the client has requested the disclosure, so the accountant may provide the information, ideally after confirming the authority in writing. The other options do not reflect the facts.

questions.question_text: In which of the following situations does the Code recognise that a professional accountant has a professional duty or right to disclose confidential information, even without the client's consent?

options.A: When complying with a quality review by ICAEW, or when protecting the accountant's professional interests in legal proceedings
options.B: When a journalist asks for information about a client's tax affairs
options.C: When a competitor of the client offers to pay for the information
options.D: When a friend asks for advice about investing in the client

questions.explanation: The Code recognises a professional duty or right to disclose in certain circumstances, including complying with the quality review of a professional body, responding to an inquiry or investigation by a professional or regulatory body, protecting the accountant's interests in legal proceedings, and complying with technical and ethical standards. Disclosures to journalists, competitors or friends do not fall into these categories.

questions.question_text: Money laundering is often described in three stages: placement, layering and integration. A criminal moves illegally obtained funds through a series of transfers between bank accounts in different countries to hide their origin. Which stage does this represent?

options.A: Placement
options.B: Integration
options.C: Structuring
options.D: Layering

questions.explanation: Placement is introducing criminal cash into the financial system. Layering involves complex transactions designed to disguise the source of the funds and break the audit trail, such as multiple international transfers. Integration is when the funds re-enter the legitimate economy, for example through property purchases, appearing to be legitimate.

questions.question_text: An accountant has made an internal report of suspected money laundering about a client to the firm's money laundering reporting officer (MLRO). The client then asks the accountant why the firm has delayed a transaction. What should the accountant do?

options.A: Explain to the client that a suspicious activity report has been made
options.B: Avoid saying anything that might alert the client to the report or any investigation, and seek guidance from the MLRO
options.C: Ask the client directly whether the funds came from criminal activity
options.D: Withdraw the report so that the transaction can proceed

questions.explanation: Disclosing to the client that a report has been made, or that an investigation may be under way, could amount to the offence of tipping off and could prejudice an investigation. The accountant should be careful in communications and seek guidance from the MLRO. Asking the client directly about criminal funds also risks tipping them off.

questions.question_text: Under UK anti-money laundering rules, an employee in an accountancy firm who suspects that a client is laundering money should normally report the suspicion to whom?

options.A: The client's finance director
options.B: The firm's money laundering reporting officer (MLRO)
options.C: The client's external auditors
options.D: The financial press

questions.explanation: Employees in the regulated sector should report suspicions internally to their firm's MLRO, who decides whether to make a suspicious activity report to the National Crime Agency. Reporting to the client or third parties could amount to tipping off. Accountants have a responsibility to help detect and prevent criminal activity such as money laundering.

questions.question_text: The ICAEW Code of Ethics includes provisions on responding to non-compliance with laws and regulations (NOCLAR). What is the main purpose of these provisions?

options.A: To require accountants to investigate and prosecute all breaches of law themselves
options.B: To guide accountants on how to respond, in the public interest, when they become aware of actual or suspected breaches of laws and regulations by clients or employers
options.C: To prevent accountants from ever discussing suspected breaches with management
options.D: To ensure that accountants ignore minor breaches of any law

questions.explanation: The NOCLAR provisions set out how an accountant should respond when they encounter non-compliance or suspected non-compliance, including understanding the matter, discussing it with an appropriate level of management, and considering whether further action, such as disclosure to an appropriate authority, is needed in the public interest. Accountants are not expected to act as investigators or prosecutors. Clearly inconsequential matters are outside the scope of the provisions.

questions.question_text: Independence is often described as having two elements. What are they?

options.A: Independence of mind and independence in appearance
options.B: Financial independence and legal independence
options.C: Personal independence and political independence
options.D: Independence of fees and independence of location

questions.explanation: Independence of mind is the state of mind that allows a conclusion to be reached without being affected by influences that compromise professional judgement. Independence in appearance means avoiding facts and circumstances that would lead a reasonable and informed third party to conclude that integrity, objectivity or professional scepticism has been compromised. Both are important for assurance engagements.

questions.question_text: An accountancy firm is asked to advise two clients who are both bidding to acquire the same company. What ethical issue does this create?

options.A: A conflict of interest
options.B: A breach of professional competence
options.C: A money laundering offence
options.D: A self-review threat

questions.explanation: A conflict of interest arises when a firm provides services to two or more clients whose interests are in conflict regarding the same matter. Advising competing bidders could compromise objectivity and confidentiality. The firm must identify and evaluate the conflict and decide whether it can be addressed or whether it must decline one or both engagements.

questions.question_text: A firm decides it can act for two clients whose interests conflict over the same matter. Which combination of measures is most appropriate to address the conflict?

options.A: Disclosing the conflict to both clients and obtaining their consent, using separate engagement teams, and putting in place information barriers
options.B: Keeping the conflict secret from both clients to protect confidentiality
options.C: Using the same engagement team for both clients to improve efficiency
options.D: Charging a higher fee to both clients

questions.explanation: Where a conflict of interest can be managed, appropriate measures include disclosing the nature of the conflict and obtaining consent from the relevant parties, and using separate teams with clear policies to protect confidentiality. Keeping the conflict secret or using a single team would increase the threat. Fee levels do not address the conflict.

questions.question_text: A finance manager's bonus depends on the company reporting profit above a target, and she is responsible for estimating a large provision. Which threat to the fundamental principles does this create?

options.A: Self-review threat
options.B: Advocacy threat
options.C: Self-interest threat
options.D: Familiarity threat

questions.explanation: A self-interest threat is the threat that a financial or other interest will inappropriately influence an accountant's judgement or behaviour. Her bonus gives her a personal incentive to understate the provision. Safeguards include independent review of the estimate by someone without a similar incentive.

questions.question_text: An accountancy firm designs a client's inventory valuation system and then audits the inventory figures produced by that system. Which threat arises?

options.A: Intimidation threat
options.B: Advocacy threat
options.C: Self-review threat
options.D: Self-interest threat

questions.explanation: A self-review threat arises when an accountant evaluates the results of their own or their firm's previous work. The audit team may not appropriately evaluate a system the firm designed. This is a key reason why some non-audit services are restricted for audit clients.

questions.question_text: An audit manager has worked on the same client for many years and has become close friends with the client's finance director. Which threat is most likely to arise?

options.A: Self-review threat
options.B: Advocacy threat
options.C: Self-interest threat
options.D: Familiarity threat

questions.explanation: A familiarity threat arises when, because of a long or close relationship, an accountant becomes too sympathetic to the client's interests or too accepting of their work. Safeguards include rotating senior staff and having the work reviewed by someone not involved in the engagement.

questions.question_text: An accountant in practice is asked by a client to represent it publicly in a dispute with a tax authority, promoting the client's position. Which threat arises?

options.A: Familiarity threat
options.B: Advocacy threat
options.C: Self-review threat
options.D: Intimidation threat

questions.explanation: An advocacy threat arises when an accountant promotes a client's or employer's position to the point that their objectivity is compromised. Acting on a client's behalf in a dispute can create this threat. For audit clients, such services may be restricted because of their effect on independence.

questions.question_text: A company's chief executive tells the financial controller that she will lose her job unless she agrees to an accounting treatment that she considers inappropriate. Which threat is this?

options.A: Advocacy threat
options.B: Familiarity threat
options.C: Self-review threat
options.D: Intimidation threat

questions.explanation: An intimidation threat is the threat that an accountant will be deterred from acting objectively because of actual or perceived pressures, including attempts to exercise undue influence. Threatening dismissal is a clear example. The controller should not give in to the pressure and should consider raising the matter with those charged with governance or seeking advice.

questions.question_text: Under the conceptual framework in the ICAEW Code of Ethics, what are the three main steps an accountant should follow when dealing with threats to the fundamental principles?

options.A: Ignore minor threats, report major threats, and resign
options.B: Calculate threats, disclose threats, and insure against threats
options.C: Identify threats, evaluate threats, and address threats
options.D: Delegate threats, document threats, and accept threats

questions.explanation: The conceptual framework requires accountants to identify threats to compliance with the fundamental principles, evaluate whether they are at an acceptable level, and address them by eliminating them or reducing them to an acceptable level. Where that is not possible, the accountant should decline or end the relevant service or activity.

questions.question_text: When evaluating whether a threat to the fundamental principles is at an acceptable level, which test does the ICAEW Code of Ethics require an accountant to apply?

options.A: The balance of probabilities test
options.B: The reasonable and informed third party test
options.C: The going concern test
options.D: The materiality threshold of 5% of profit

questions.explanation: An acceptable level is one at which an accountant using the reasonable and informed third party test would likely conclude that the accountant complies with the fundamental principles. The test considers whether a hypothetical person with relevant knowledge, weighing all the facts, would reach the same conclusion. Legal and accounting tests such as the balance of probabilities and going concern are not used for this purpose.

questions.question_text: How do the ethical threats typically faced by professional accountants in business tend to differ from those faced by accountants in public practice?

options.A: Accountants in business never face self-interest threats
options.B: Accountants in business are more likely to face pressure from their own employer, for example from managers whose interests depend on reported results, and may find it harder to walk away because their livelihood depends on one organisation
options.C: Only accountants in public practice face intimidation threats
options.D: Accountants in business are not required to comply with the fundamental principles

questions.explanation: Accountants in business often face pressure from superiors and colleagues to present results favourably, and their employment and income depend on a single employer, which can make intimidation and self-interest threats harder to resist. Accountants in practice face threats arising from client relationships and fees. All professional accountants must comply with the fundamental principles.

questions.question_text: An employee reports serious wrongdoing at her employer to an appropriate regulator after internal reporting has failed. Which statement about whistleblowing in the UK is correct?

options.A: Whistleblowers have no legal protection in the UK
options.B: Whistleblowing is always a breach of confidentiality and results in disciplinary action by ICAEW
options.C: Whistleblowing law requires employees to report all concerns to the media first
options.D: The Public Interest Disclosure Act 1998 can protect workers who make qualifying disclosures from dismissal or detriment, although whistleblowers may still experience personal stress and strained working relationships

questions.explanation: The Public Interest Disclosure Act 1998 provides protection for workers who make protected disclosures in the public interest, for example to their employer or to a prescribed person such as a regulator. Even with legal protection, speaking out can have a significant personal impact, including stress and damaged relationships. Disclosure to the media is protected only in limited circumstances and is not the first step.

questions.topic: Data ethics and the impact of technology
questions.question_text: Which of the following is a principle commonly included in frameworks for the ethical use of data?

options.A: Collecting as much data as possible in case it is useful later
options.B: Keeping data subjects unaware of how their data is used
options.C: Transparency about how data is collected and used
options.D: Sharing data with any party willing to pay for it

questions.explanation: Data ethics frameworks commonly include principles such as transparency, accountability and fairness. Individuals should understand how their data is collected and used. Collecting excessive data, hiding its use or selling it indiscriminately all conflict with these principles.

questions.topic: Data ethics and the impact of technology
questions.question_text: A company collects customers' dates of birth, home addresses and employment details when it only needs an email address to send a newsletter. Which data protection principle is it failing to apply?

options.A: Data minimisation
options.B: Accuracy
options.C: Storage limitation
options.D: Integrity and confidentiality

questions.explanation: Data minimisation requires personal data to be adequate, relevant and limited to what is necessary for the purposes for which it is processed. Collecting detailed personal information to send a newsletter goes beyond what is needed. The other principles relate to keeping data correct, not keeping it longer than necessary, and keeping it secure.

questions.topic: Data ethics and the impact of technology
questions.question_text: A company collected customers' personal data to process deliveries. It now wants to use the same data, without telling customers, to build profiles for a third party's marketing campaigns. Which data protection principle does this most directly breach?

options.A: Data minimisation
options.B: Purpose limitation
options.C: Storage limitation
options.D: Accuracy

questions.explanation: Purpose limitation requires personal data to be collected for specified, explicit and legitimate purposes and not further processed in a way that is incompatible with those purposes. Using delivery data for third-party marketing without informing customers is an incompatible new purpose. It would also raise concerns about transparency and fairness.

questions.topic: Data ethics and the impact of technology
questions.question_text: A bank trains an algorithm to assess loan applications using historical lending decisions, which had disadvantaged applicants from certain postcodes. What is the main ethical risk?

options.A: The algorithm will be unable to process any applications
options.B: The algorithm will automatically remove all bias from future decisions
options.C: The algorithm will breach copyright law
options.D: The algorithm may reproduce and reinforce the historical bias in its decisions

questions.explanation: Data bias occurs when the data used to train or inform a system is unrepresentative or reflects past discrimination. An algorithm trained on biased decisions is likely to repeat those patterns, leading to unfair outcomes. Accountants should challenge how data is selected and captured, and how outputs are tested for bias.

questions.topic: Data ethics and the impact of technology
questions.question_text: A management accountant is given sustainability data from a supplier to include in the company's report. Which action best reflects the need to maintain an enquiring mind?

options.A: Including the data as received because the supplier is a long-standing partner
options.B: Considering the source and reliability of the data, how it was collected, and whether it is consistent with other information
options.C: Excluding all supplier data from the report
options.D: Rounding all the figures to make them look more consistent

questions.explanation: An enquiring mind involves evaluating information from a variety of sources and perspectives, considering its reliability, completeness and consistency before relying on it. A long relationship does not guarantee accuracy. Excluding data without assessment, or adjusting it cosmetically, would not produce reliable information.

questions.topic: Data ethics and the impact of technology
questions.question_text: A company uses a complex artificial intelligence (AI) model to make credit decisions, but cannot explain to rejected applicants why they were declined. Which ethical issue is most directly raised?

options.A: Lack of transparency and explainability
options.B: Data minimisation
options.C: Self-review threat
options.D: Lack of storage capacity

questions.explanation: Many AI systems operate as 'black boxes', making it hard to explain how decisions are reached. This undermines transparency and accountability, makes bias difficult to detect, and can prevent individuals from challenging decisions that affect them. Explainability is a key consideration in the ethical use of AI.

questions.topic: Data ethics and the impact of technology
questions.question_text: An accountant uses an AI tool to draft a client's disclosure notes. The draft looks professional but cites an accounting standard requirement that does not exist. Which statement best describes the accountant's responsibility?

options.A: The AI provider is fully responsible for any errors, so the accountant need not check the output
options.B: The accountant should use the output as long as it looks professional
options.C: The accountant remains responsible for the work and must review and verify AI-generated output before relying on it
options.D: The accountant must stop using all technology in their work

questions.explanation: Professional competence and due care requires accountants to understand the limitations of the tools they use and to review their output. Generative AI can produce plausible but incorrect content, so over-reliance creates a risk of automation bias and errors. Responsibility for the work remains with the accountant; banning all technology is not required.

questions.topic: Data ethics and the impact of technology
questions.question_text: What is the main purpose of data protection legislation such as the UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018?

options.A: To allow organisations to sell personal data without restriction
options.B: To protect companies' trade secrets from competitors
options.C: To set accounting standards for intangible assets
options.D: To protect individuals' rights over their personal data and to set rules for how organisations process it

questions.explanation: Data protection legislation gives individuals rights over their personal data and requires organisations to process it lawfully, fairly and transparently, keep it secure and use it only for legitimate purposes. Commercially sensitive information such as trade secrets is protected through other means, including contracts and confidentiality obligations.

questions.topic: Data ethics and the impact of technology
questions.question_text: A trainee pastes a client's unpublished financial forecasts into a free public generative AI tool to help write a summary. Which is the main ethical concern?

options.A: The summary may be too short
options.B: The AI tool may round the figures differently from the client
options.C: Confidential client information may be disclosed to, stored or used by a third party without authority, breaching confidentiality
options.D: The trainee will be committing a money laundering offence

questions.explanation: Entering confidential information into a public AI tool may mean it is stored, processed or used to train the model by a third party, which could amount to unauthorised disclosure. This risks breaching the principle of confidentiality and possibly data protection law. Firms should have policies on approved tools and on what information may be entered into them.

questions.topic: Data ethics and the impact of technology
questions.question_text: Which of the following is an ethical issue arising from the development and use of new technology in finance functions?

options.A: Faster processing of routine transactions
options.B: Deepfake audio or video being used to impersonate senior managers and authorise fraudulent payments
options.C: Improved accuracy in reconciling bank accounts
options.D: Lower costs of storing documents

questions.explanation: Technology brings benefits such as speed, accuracy and lower costs, but also raises ethical issues including fraud risks such as deepfakes, cyber security, privacy, bias and job displacement. Accountants need to apply professional scepticism, for example by verifying unusual payment requests through independent channels.
